name: Igal
overview: Igal was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, known primarily for his role as one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. His participation as a spy highlights his significance within the Israelite community during their wilderness journey. The Scriptures specifically note his tribal affiliation and his involvement in this important reconnaissance mission.
namesAndTitles: The name Igal means 'he redeems,' a proper name that does not appear to have been given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a general biblical theme of redemption, though the text does not elaborate further on its significance for this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Igal was a son of Joseph, which situates him within the broader family lineage of Israel. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Igal's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his selection as one of the twelve spies representing the tribes of Israel during the critical moment of scouting the Promised Land. His inclusion among the spies from Issachar underscores the tribe's involvement in God's unfolding plan for Israel. While the biblical record is brief, Igal's role contributes to the larger story of Israel's journey and God's promises to His people.
